nary_nodes.label: Victory parade in Madrid
evidence: Spain's newly crowned World Cup champions were greeted by a million fans as the team arrived for the victory parade in Madrid.

The players, some shirtless, others holding drinks, set off on their procession along the main arteries in the city centre where a sea of fans in red and yellow were waiting, with the destination Cibeles square.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A parade is a public celebration, best matched by Festival.

nary_nodes.label: Spain 1-0 victory over Argentina
evidence: Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in New Jersey on Sunday, secured by a Ferran Torres strike in extra-time, has sparked an outpouring of national pride in the football-mad country, whose only other World Cup triumph came in 2010.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A match between national teams is a sports event.

nary_nodes.label: Rodri holds World Cup trophy
evidence: Spain captain Rodri held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs as he descended from the Iberia plane that flew the team home after clinching their second star.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A trophy presentation is a generic event; the generic Event class fits best.

nary_nodes.label: 13-year-old boy killed in Ciudad Rodrigo
evidence: On a tragic note, a 13-year-old boy was killed around midnight in the town of Ciudad Rodrigo in the west, after a fountain crumbled under the weight of supporters who had climbed onto it to celebrate.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A tragedy is a generic occurrence; use the generic Event class.

nary_nodes.label: King praises team
evidence: “You have shown your grit, your resilience and your courage, always backed by your technical skill, your control and command of the game, combining head and heart,” the king told La Roja’s stars.

nary_nodes.label: Rodri on winning
evidence: “I’ve always said it, winning with your country is the most beautiful thing there is, above all a World Cup,” said Rodri.

nary_nodes.label: Sanchez on record
evidence: “It’s two for two,” said Sanchez, of Spain’s record in World Cup finals. “Why not dream of a third in 2030, especially with Spain as hosts?”

nary_nodes.label: Marca praises team
evidence: “The kings of all-time!” wrote Marca, celebrating a “second star that will now be stitched onto the Spanish jersey after yet another masterclass in collective play”.

nary_nodes.label: Messi on loss
evidence: “The pain is immense, and it’s going to be hard for this wound to heal,” Messi wrote on Instagram.
